quote: I think I was calling Kenny. Is Kenny there?
stewart_read: The intro never establishes ION as a company or references a lead source; customer's confusion about who he's even talking to is the direct consequence.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep could be relying on a prior touch with Kenny to carry legitimacy, but nothing in the transcript confirms that context was reinforced.
coaching_implication: Open with company name + lead source ('This is Nefer with ION Solar, following up on your conversation with Kenny') instead of leading with just a first name.

quote: I'm gonna need a new roof. So
stewart_read: Customer states his entry point to solar is a roof replacement — a direct trigger for the roofing bridge — and rep only says 'I wanna see what this looks like,' filing it instead of bridging.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may be deferring the roofing conversation to the specialist deliberately, but there's no verbal bridge or mention of Ion's roofing team anywhere in the call to support that being intentional.
coaching_implication: Should have said something like 'Ion actually does roofing in-house — we can look at pairing that with solar' to capture both the roof and solar revenue paths.

quote: I was exploring the solar roofs, so I don't know what that looks like. It looks like they have their own shingles that are solar panels
stewart_read: Customer is describing Tesla solar roof tiles, a product Ion does not sell — this is exactly the expectation gap the schema flags, and the rep never reframes it.
alternative_hypothesis: Rep may correctly be leaving product-mix explanation to the closer, which is schema-consistent (closer handles product mix) — this softens the miss.
coaching_implication: A single line clarifying Ion's actual roofing/solar offering versus the shingle-tile product he's describing would prevent a mismatched expectation heading into the closer call.

quote: Oh, jeez. Okay. We can definitely help out there.
stewart_read: Rep captures the $250 bill figure and reacts verbally but never flips it into an emotional anchor against the utility or ties it forward to the appointment's value.
coaching_implication: Should reflect the number back as leverage: 'so $250 a month straight to Dominion with nothing to show for it — that's exactly what we'll target in the design.'

quote: I just bought the house April 16.
stewart_read: Customer has no usage history since he just moved in; rep correctly accepts this and pivots to square footage rather than pushing further — an appropriate adaptation, not a failure.
coaching_implication: No action needed here; rep's move to alternate data (square footage) was the right call given the genuine gap.

quote: Yeah. Then we can give you a call around this time, two, 02:30.
stewart_read: The appointment time is proposed and accepted but the call closes without the 'is that fair' handshake, one-hour block statement, or no-driving/text-followup promise.
coaching_implication: Close with the full button-up checklist to lock the appointment procedurally, not just verbally.
